financial_summary: Prairiesky Royalty Ltd. is a mid-cap energy business with a $5.7B market cap on $338M of annual revenue.

The top line has compounded at -12% over the past three years, and a shrinking top line is the hardest headwind any business can overcome. Operating margins are contracting by -2.8pp, the first warning that competitive pressure is eroding the franchise.
Returns on capital run at 8% against a 8% cost of capital, which means the business barely earns its keep economically. Gross margins of 71% confirm genuine pricing power.

The business throws off $182M in free cash flow — roughly 54 cents on every revenue dollar, which is the owner-earnings figure that actually belongs to shareholders, and cash conversion sits at 1.74× so those profits are backed by real cash.
On the balance sheet, leverage is comfortably conservative at 0.6× net debt/EBITDA, and interest coverage of 21× is fortress-like.

Shareholder yield of 3.0% reflects a genuine commitment to returning capital rather than empire-building, and insider ownership is negligible, so management has little personal stake in the long-term outcome, and within its sector the business captures 5.4× its fair share of profits, a structural advantage visible in the numbers.
